thread.title: Tech Today: A Micron Blowout? Defending Facebook, Dumping Oracle - Barron's

author: Tiernan Ray
title: Tech Today: A Micron Blowout? Defending Facebook, Dumping Oracle - Barron's
text:
Here are some things going on today in your world of tech :
Defending Facebook
Shares of Facebook ( FB ) are down $4.98, or 3%, at $167.58, as the company continues to deal with fallout from having given consulting firm Cambridge Analytica inappropriate access to user data.
The latest development is a Bloomberg note this morning saying the U.S. Federal Trade Commission is “probing” the company to determine if it “violated terms of a consent decree of its use of personal data,” citing one unnamed source.
But multiple analysts are stepping up to champion the social network.
Credit Suisse ’s Stephen Ju reiterates an Outperform rating, and a $240 price target, writing that he expects the stock will have "further headline risk in the coming weeks as senior management is summoned to DC for hearings with lawmakers."
Nevertheless, he’s still a buyer, given "the current 23x P/E multiple on GAAP NTM EPS already reflects risks.” That multiple is "also in-line with the low-end of the recent trading range – when shares struggled with greater questions around revenue growth given the move to slow down ad load/inventory growth."
And Merrill Lynch ’s Justin Post keeps his Buy rating, and $265 price target, writing the stock is “oversold,” even if he expects that “sentiment could remain pressured."
For more on the Facebook morass, see the essay this morning by my colleague Jon Swartz.
Dumping Oracle
Shares of Oracle ( ORCL ) are are down $4.78, or 9%, at $47.17, extending last night’s losses, after the company’s fiscal Q3 revenue came in slightly below consensus, and its forecast for revenue this quarter was well below consensus.
The stock has gotten at least two downgrades this morning, that I can see, from Stifel Nicolaus and Merrill Lynch , both cutting the stock to the equivalent of a Hold rating.
Stifel’s Brad Reback , keeping his $53 target on the stock, writes that “we find the lackluster results/guidance concerning, especially in contrast to the strong results posted by Microsoft, SalesForce.com, Adobe, Workday, ServiceNow, Splunk, Nutanix, etc. driven by one of the best software spending environments we have seen since picking up coverage of the space in 2001."
Defending Universal Display
Shares of organic light-emitting diode tech maker Universal Display ( OLED ) are $6.70, or 6%, at $115.70, bouncing back from yesterday’s 12% drop, prompted by that Bloomberg article speculating Apple ( AAPL ) is developing its own display technology for the iPhone, called “ micro LED ,” which would presumably crimp demand for AMOLED displays that Universal makes money off of.
But some bulls are coming to Unviersal’s defense today. Goldman Sachs ’s Brian Lee reiterates a Buy rating and a $190 price target, writing that his conversations with people in the micro LED "supply chain" suggest to him that "visibility remains low on potential for commercialization, let alone on timing."
Hence, "we see risk-reward at 12X implied 'peak EPS' for OLED shares as attractive as it’s been for some time."
A Micron blow-out?
Another day, another price target increase for Micron Technology ( MU ).
Credit Suisse ’s John Pitzer reiterates an Outperform rating, and raises his price target to $70 from $60, writing that when the company reports results this Thursday , after the closing bell, it may forecast Q3’s revenue in a range of $7.5 billion to $7.7 billion, well above current consensus of $7.25 billion.
Looking past the quarter, Pitzer writes that it is “important to note” that this year, investment in Micron is "more dependent” on demand than supply . On that score, "We continue to see more sustainable demand drivers in DataCenter where high utilization rates significantly increases DRAM ROI – China new entrants and 3D XPoint as a substitute for DRAM need to be monitored."
Micron shares are up 68 cents, or 1%, at $60.82.
Another vote for II-VI
Shares of fiber-optic component maker II-VI ( IIVI ) are up $1.95, or 4.4%, at $47.15, as the stock gets yet another in a spate of positive views, this one from B. Riley FBR ’s Dave Kang , who raises his rating to Buy from Neutral and raises his price target to $50 from $40.50, after gaining newfound confidence at last week’s OFC trade show.
His takeaways from the show were that "demand for industrial lasers remains strong,” "Chinese demand for the company’s optical products has improved meaningfully in recent weeks," and “long-term growth opportunities in SiC [silicon carbide] and 3DS [3-D sensing] remain compelling."
D.A. Davidson ’s Thomas Diffely started coverage of II-VI last Thursday at Buy, with a $55 target; and Deutsche Bank 's Vishal Shah started coverage yesterday with a Buy rating, and a $56 price target.
Dumping Qorvo
Shares of wireless chip maker Qorvo ( QRVO ) are down $2.32, or 3%, at $76.10, after Instinet ’s Krysten Sciacca cut her rating on the shares to Neutral from Buy, after talking with contacts in Taiwan, and coming away with the impression that "Qorvo may have less share than originally forecasted in the mid/high-band PAD for the next-gen LCD iPhone.”
That is the version of the iPhone expected to have features of the iPhone X, but with a plain old LCD screen . Sciacca now believes that Broadcom ( AVGO ) has taken some of the business away.
"We now believe both AVGO and QRVO will supply the mid/high-band PAD to this SKU, with AVGO having majority share."
"We note Anne Lee now estimates the RF BOM for the next-gen 6.1” LCD iPhone to be USD 22 versus their prior est. of USD 20. The price increase likely signals Broadcom has won some share in mid/high-band PAD socket."
